subject: Clarify billing quantum and how minimums apply to long-context pilots

Subject: Clarify how billing floor affects pilot (long-context session)

Hi Logan,

Quick question from procurement: our pilot is going to hit a lot of long-context conversations (some threads ~12k tokens). The pricing sheet mentions a "billing quantum" and a per-request minimum — can you confirm how those interact with long contexts and streaming responses?

Specifically: if a single request consumes 12k tokens on a model that has a 6k-context quantum, is that billed as two quanta, or are there rounding/minimum rules that could make the effective billed units higher? Also worried about repeated small replies in the same session — do they get aggregated or billed separately?

We need a short, worked example so procurement can sign off on the pilot pricing.

Thanks,
Rachel
Rachel Adams
Director of Platform Engineering, ScaleApps
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Clarify how billing floor affects pilot (long-context session)

Hey Rachel — thanks for the clear question, happy to spell it out. TL;DR: we bill on model-quantum boundaries with a per-request minimum that can interact with context slicing; however KV/prefix caching and session aggregation can reduce duplicate billing for repeated short replies in the same conversation. A short worked example below.

How billing works (plain language):
- Quantum and per-request minimum: each request is evaluated against the model's quantum (e.g., 6k token quantum for Model-A). If a request's token usage exceeds one quantum, we break the request into quanta-sized execution chunks for scheduling and metering. Billing rounds up to whole quanta.
- Minimum charge / per-call floor: there is a minimum billable unit per call (e.g., 0.5 quantum) which only affects very small calls — it does not stack multiplicatively per chunk.
- Session aggregation: requests within an active session can be aggregated for KV/prefix reuse. If the same prefix/kernel is reused, the effective billed tokens can be lower because we credit KV cache reuse. This is not automatic across independent API keys without session linking.

Worked example (Model-A: 6k quantum, per-call floor = 0.5 quantum):
- Single 12,000-token request: engine slices into two 6k quanta -> billed as 2 quanta.
- Same 12,000 token broken into a 8k prompt + 4k generated tokens in a single call -> still 12k total, billed as 2 quanta.
- Many short replies in a single session: if each reply is 300 tokens and KV/prefix reuse is effective, the first reply may incur the per-call floor (0.5 quantum) but subsequent replies may be charged for incremental tokens or get reduced effective cost because of caching.

Open items — want to confirm with you:
1) Which model are you planning to run for the pilot (Model-A or Model-B)? Model-B has 8k quantum and different rounding.
2) Expected distribution: are most long threads single large requests or many small turns? If you can share a sample distribution we can run a spreadsheet.

I can send a worked spreadsheet and a line item mock invoice. Vanessa, can you chime in on how committed-discount mechanics would layer on top (commit tiers vs per-quantum discounts)?

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Adams <rachel.adams@scaleapps.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-05-19T10:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify billing quantum and how minimums apply to long-context pilots

Thanks Logan. Quick additions from pricing side:
- Discount stacking: discounts apply to the billed quanta after rounding. For example, if the raw billed units are 2 quanta and you have a 20% committed discount at the tier that covers the pilot, the invoice will show 2 quanta at list then a 20% line discount.
- Minimums and first-month concessions: procurement often worries about first-month spikes. For pilots we can offer a one-time waiver of per-call minimums up to a threshold (e.g., waive floors for up to 250k tokens in month 1) or provide an adjustable pilot credit if you prefer predictable spend.
- Long-context fragmentation: when requests exceed a quantum we do not apply the per-call floor separately to each internal execution chunk. The per-call floor applies to the logical API call; chunking only affects how we schedule and may affect cache efficiency.

I'll attach a small workbook that shows three scenarios: single 12k request, 12k as repeated short replies, and a mixed pattern. We also show invoice line formatting so procurement sees how discounts appear.

Vanessa
Director, GTM Pricing, Redwood Inference

Rachel, team — attaching the workbook and a proposed MAP (mutual action plan) that includes the one-time waiver language. Quick answers inline and a numeric worked example below. Also added a calendar link to schedule Wed 2029-05-22 10:00 PT (or the link if you prefer another time).

Numeric worked example (Model-A, 6k quantum, per-call floor 0.5 quantum, list price per quantum = $0.12 per token-quantum equivalent => we show per-quantum price as $720):
- Single 12k call: billed quanta = 2; list charge = 2 * $720 = $1,440.
- Apply committed discount 20% = $288 discount.
- Final charge = $1,152 (per-call floor not applicable above 1 quantum).

Aborted streaming scenario: billed tokens are the tokens consumed before abort; we bill for consumed tokens rounded up to quanta boundaries (or to per-call floor if under the floor). In your example: if you stream and abort at 9k, billed quanta = ceil(9k / 6k) = 2 quanta (so you would be billed for 2 quanta). For this reason, if you expect frequent early-abort patterns we can discuss smaller quantum model variants or a pilot credit to offset initial inefficiency.

Waiver language (proposed): "Redwood will waive per-call minimums for billed usage up to 250,000 tokens during Customer’s first invoice month for the ScaleApps pilot (Deal SCL-4987). Waiver applies to per-call floors only and does not change quantum rounding rules."
